<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**20** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `669ddac4f5a113f6bcf218a005b46f36d2104a5b` — the merge of head `692c9c1b8c66cb99b6265edae19527169284652c` into base `4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 669ddac4f5a113f6bcf218a005b46f36d2104a5b && git checkout 669ddac4f5a113f6bcf218a005b46f36d2104a5b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9 692c9c1b8c66cb99b6265edae19527169284652c && git checkout -B drift-repro 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9 && git merge --no-ff 692c9c1b8c66cb99b6265edae19527169284652c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: 82b53be53cc3e0f2818cd8a42ca536509e33b54d

This is the first L1 read of #34992 (card #34921) at the head above. The base is fb5c42d10, and the head merges cleanly with current main.

## Must-fix

None.

## Should-fix

- **S1: amend the claim surface to name the rest test file.** No head move is needed. `packages/rest/src/system-overview-dataset-vocabulary.test.ts` is a new file in a package the claim (6961389476) does not name. The pin-test slot names `packages/services/service-analytics` dataset-tools / term-matcher tests "or platform-objects tests", with the clause "wherever the System Overview datasets reach `list_datasets` without new wiring". The choice itself is sound:
  - `packages/rest` already depends on both `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/service-analytics`, so no new wiring is needed;
  - it is the one place the real datasets, the real bundle and the real executor meet.

  Still, the claim names two packages and the PR adds a test in a third. One amendment line on the card naming this file closes it.

## Notes

- **Shape.** `Fixes #34921`; 25 files, +907 −78, mostly bundle rows. `check-governed-merges --pr 34992`: 0 of 25 paths are governed and the PR has 985 lines, so it is not Tier H.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch. That is the only package whose src moved; `packages/rest` is test-only. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` match the claim. Members gain values on keys the spec already declares (`synonyms`, `description`; `dataset-tools.zod.ts`, `translation.zod.ts`), with no schema, protocol or rule change, so this is ui-only and Clause-② no. L1 is the review of record, and no L2 is owed.
- **Scope against acceptance.**
  - All seven members declare `synonyms` in one authored array, Chinese and English together, with no bundle (ADR-0149 D1), and each has a one-sentence `description`.
  - Each description has a bundle row in all 11 locales, with source-hash rows in the 10 translated ones.
  - I spot-read de, ja-JP, zh-CN and zh-Hant: they are real translations, and they agree with the English on "active or not" and on the System bucket.
  - The rest pin covers both `['用户数']` and `['how many users']`, in en and zh-CN, through `translateDataset` and the real `list_datasets`. Each resolves to `sys_user_metrics.measures.user_count` alone, `matchedOn: 'synonym'`, with no candidates.
  - The control `['营收','revenue']` misses.
  - The zh-CN catalogue serves the bundled description.
  - The i18n baseline moved 0, which the PR body states with its reason (the extract config declares no datasets). That satisfies "states by how much".
- **Platform-objects pins.** Every member has a Han and a Latin synonym plus a description. The full `DatasetSchema` parse passes. A cross-dataset, every-locale collision check finds no synonym equal to another measure's name, served label or synonym. The en bundle copies each source description verbatim, and no translated locale serves the English source.
- **Ablation.** The PR records that removing user_count's synonyms turns 4 tests red, and that the blob is restored to HEAD.
- **Nit, `package_count`.** The file comment says "the other language's label is listed too (`users` beside 「用户」)". That holds for user, org, session and event, but not for `package_count`: its zh-CN label 「安装」 is not among its synonyms, while 'installations' is. If leaving it out is deliberate (「安装」 alone is ambiguous), a few words in the comment would say so. Otherwise add it; the collision pin would judge it.
- **Nit, 「用户」.** Under zh-CN, 「用户」 matches the `user_count` synonym and also the `user_id` dimension label. The file comment says it still answers with `user_count`, which follows the selection rule in `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` ("A dimension match alone picks a grouping, not a number: a measure must still match"). It is the most likely word an admin types, so a one-leg pin of `listFor('zh-CN', ['用户'])` would hold that reading. Optional.
- **CI at this head.** When I read it, 17 checks were green and the Test Core shards, Type Check and Build Core were still running. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` each show one cancelled run, superseded by the body edit, with a fresh run in progress. Landing waits on them.
